title: Viniyoga of the prāṇāyāma

words.role: the first mantra of the prāṇāyāma
with the seer’s name: ‘the seer is …’

words.meaning: gāyatrī, the metre of three lines of eight syllables
of the seven vyāhṛtis beginning with bhūḥ
Atri, Bhṛgu, Kutsa, Vasiṣṭha, Gautama, Kāśyapa and Aṅgiras
words.role: the seers, one for each vyāhṛti in order

words.meaning: gāyatrī, uṣṇih, anuṣṭubh, bṛhatī, paṅkti, triṣṭubh and jagatī
words.role: the seven metres, one for each vyāhṛti

words.meaning: Agni, Vāyu, Arka (the Sun), Vāgīśa (Bṛhaspati), Varuṇa, Indra and the All-gods
in the prāṇāyāma, the restraint of breath

words.role: what the mantra is used for

sandhi.rule: a visarga after i becomes r before a voiced consonant

samasa.vigraha: भूः आदिः यासां ताः सप्त व्याहृतयः
samasa.meaning: the seven vyāhṛtis that begin with bhūḥ

samasa.members: अत्रि + भृगु + कुत्स + वसिष्ठ + गौतम + काश्यप + अङ्गिरस्

morphology.note: S writes the members of the dvandvas with hyphens and without sandhi between them (गायत्री-उष्णिक्, काश्यप-अङ्गिरस); the padaccheda keeps them as printed.

translation.literal: Of the praṇava, Brahmā the seer, divine gāyatrī the metre, the supreme Self the deity. Of the seven vyāhṛtis beginning with bhūḥ: Atri, Bhṛgu, Kutsa, Vasiṣṭha, Gautama, Kāśyapa, Aṅgiras the seers; gāyatrī, uṣṇih, anuṣṭubh, bṛhatī, paṅkti, triṣṭubh, jagatī the metres; Agni, Vāyu, Arka, Vāgīśa, Varuṇa, Indra, the All-gods the deities. The use in the prāṇāyāma.
translation.readable: For the prāṇāyāma: the praṇava — seer Brahmā, metre gāyatrī, deity the supreme Self; the seven vyāhṛtis — seven seers, seven metres and seven deities, one for each.

units.pause_note: S writes the list of metres with a pause before छन्दांसि (जगत्यः छन्दांसि), the visarga kept as at the end of a phrase; joined it would be जगत्यश्छन्दांसि.

sandhi_exceptions.note: प्रणवस्य ऋषिः: S writes the genitive and ऋषिः apart (a ṛ after -a unjoined), the usual way the viniyoga formula is said; joined it would be प्रणवस्यर्षिः.

meaning: A viniyoga is the statement said before a mantra of its seer (ṛṣi), its metre (chandas), its deity (devatā) and the use (viniyoga) it is put to. Here: the viniyoga of the whole prāṇāyāma mantra (Mahānārāyaṇa 10.35) — Om, the seven vyāhṛtis, the Gāyatrī and its ‘head’. S gives the praṇava and the vyāhṛtis; M adds the seer, metre and deity of the Gāyatrī and of its head (corrections.json). The seven lists run in parallel: the first seer, metre and deity belong to bhūḥ, the second to bhuvaḥ, and so on to satyam.
in_the_rite: Step pranava-viniyoga, before the prāṇāyāma that opens the japa, in all three services.
